_README: Committed measurements for scripts/check-token-budgets.ts. THIS IS A RATCHET, NOT A CONFIG.
Each value is the measured token cost (ceil(utf8Bytes(JSON.stringify(response))/4)) of one MCP
tool scenario, produced by invoking that tool's REGISTERED HANDLER against a contract-maximal
fixture. The declared BUDGET for each scenario lives next to its fixture in the script, with the
derivation of the number written beside it; this file records where we actually are.
measured >  budget    FAIL. The published ceiling was breached. Cut the response.
measured >  baseline  FAIL. Under the ceiling but above where we were: silent drift inside the
headroom is how a ceiling gets reached. If the increase is deliberate, run
`pnpm tsx scripts/check-token-budgets.ts --write-baseline` so the new number
lands as a reviewable diff in the SAME commit.
measured <  baseline  PASS, and it prints the delta with an instruction to lower this file in the
same commit. Failing CI on the commit that improves things is how ratchets
get deleted; a stale-high baseline cannot hide, because the delta prints on
--write-baseline REFUSES to record any value that is over its own budget. A baseline may record
where we are; it may never bless a breached ceiling.
Do not hand-edit. Regenerate with `pnpm tsx scripts/check-token-budgets.ts --write-baseline`, and
run `pnpm build` first — the script measures packages/mcp source against the built SDK/contracts.
